events.content:
Now I understand the setup. Let me look at the key issue: the project page currently fetches the title and details together with `Promise.all`, and wraps everything in a single `Suspense` boundary. The title fetch is fast, but the details fetch has an 800ms delay. To make the title appear instantly without prefetching the rest of the project page, I need to:

1. Separate the title into its own `Suspense` boundary so it renders as soon as its own data resolves, independent of the slower details.
2. Stop prefetching the project page link on the dashboard (the default `Link` prefetches).

Let me check the Next.js Link prefetch behavior and the `cacheComponents` setup to confirm the right approach. The key changes:

- On the dashboard (`app/page.tsx`): disable prefetch on the `<Link>` so navigating doesn't prefetch the project page.
- On the project page (`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`): split the title and details into separate `Suspense` boundaries so the title streams in immediately while details load independently.

Let me make these edits.

events.content:
Build succeeds. The route /projects/[slug] is now marked as Partial Prerender (◐), which confirms the streaming behavior is working correctly.

Here's what I changed and why:

## Changes

app/page.tsx — disable link prefetch
Added prefetch={false} to the project <Link>. By default, Next.js <Link> prefetches the destination route's RSC payload when the link enters the viewport. With prefetch={false}, navigating from the dashboard no longer fetches the project page ahead of time — the page is only fetched on actual navigation.

app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx — split title and details into separate Suspense boundaries

Previously, the page awaited the title and details together via Promise.all inside a single async component wrapped in one Suspense boundary. That meant the title (instant) was blocked behind the details fetch (800ms delay), so nothing appeared until both resolved.

Now there are two independent async components, each in its own Suspense boundary:
- ProjectTitle — calls only getProjectTitle(slug) (no artificial delay), so it resolves and streams in immediately.
- ProjectDetails — calls only getProjectDetails(slug) (800ms delay), streaming in afterward with its own Loading details... fallback.

Because the boundaries are siblings (not nested), the title is no longer gated on the slower details fetch. With Cache Components / Partial Prerender enabled, the static shell and the title stream first, and the details fill in as they resolve — without prefetching the full page when the dashboard link is merely visible.
